To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

positive contrast occurs when one component of a multiple schedule is changed to extinction and negative contrast occurs when it is changed to a variable-intervals schedule; that the size of the contrast depends on the duration of the less favorable component and not the duration of the more favorable component; and that the duration of each component must be at least 5 sec for contrast to be observed.
positive contrast was greater and negative contrast smaller when the duration of a component was 30 s than when it was 5 or 60 s.

the size of positive behavioral contrast is a function of the duration of the extinction component and the size of negative behavioral contrast is a positive function of the duration and a negative function of the frequency of the variable-intervall component.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of reinforcement schedules on the behavior of pigeons.
the effects of changes in one component on the behavior maintained by a multiple schedule.
the effects of reinforcement on behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
positive and negative behavioral contrast are not equivalent phenomena and that the magnitude of contrast depends on the duration of the components of multiple schedules.
the results are inconsistent with the predictions of all the theories that have been proposed to account for the phenomenon of contrast.
the results of this study are not consistent with any current theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
behavioral contrast is not a unitary phenomenon but is a complex set of effects determined by the nature of the reinforcement schedule and the conditions of reinforcement.
behavioral contrast is not an all-or-none phenomenon.
contrast is not determined by the relative frequency of reinforcement in the components but is instead a function of how much reinforcement is provided by each component.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the duration of the extinction component is the primary determinant of the magnitude of behavioral contrast.
the size of positive and negative behavioral contrast is determined by the duration of reinforcement in one of the two components of the multiple schedule.
the duration of a component that provides the most favorable conditions of reinforcement is not the main determinant of the size of contrast.
